basic_info.title: VAD: Vectorized Scene Representation for Efficient Autonomous Driving
basic_info.authors: Bo Jiang, Shaoyu Chen, Qing Xu, Bencheng Liao, Jiajie Chen, Helong Zhou, Qian Zhang, Wenyu Liu, Chang Huang, Xinggang Wang (Horizon Robotics / Huazhong University of Science and Technology)

gap_analysis.whats_missing: VAD directly inspires the transformer-encoder-over-vectorized-scene pillar (fully vectorized agents + map elements encoded with transformer/query attention), but it is an end-to-end AD planner, not a GPS map-matching method. It consumes multi-view camera features to build vectorized maps/agents on nuScenes and outputs a planned trajectory; it never ingests raw fleet GPS and performs no GPS-to-road-segment matching.
gap_analysis.novelty_vs_recombination_note: Partial overlap: the vectorized transformer scene-encoder pillar is well established here, but only for AD planning, leaving its use for label-free GPS map matching open.

relevance.bmw_relevance: Architectural inspiration only (it is cited directly in the thesis hypothesis for the vectorized transformer encoder); it operates on AD control/planning, not BMW fleet GPS analytics or map matching.
